label: Doctor advisor bridges are one per ROUTE, not per command file: scoring-compatibility.json carries 18 command-doctor-* ids in each of the typescript and python lists, and the ids map to routes (git.md -> hooks/setup/standards, skill-advisor.md -> six). A /doctor:ci surface therefore costs five ids times two platform lists = ten activation entries, plus five derived bridges; registering a single command-doctor-ci id would leave toggle and scaffold inactive.

CI vocabulary collides with spec-kit: command-spec-kit-plan is described as a planning workflow and command-spec-kit-implement as an implementation workflow, so a CI prompt carrying the bare word 'workflow' sits in spec-kit's keyword space; no bridge names GitHub Actions, workflow files or continuous integration. /doctor:ci and sk-code-ci must lead with ci/github actions/pipeline compounds and avoid the bare word workflow. Occupancy is confirmed from the registry; the misroute itself is inferred and needs one sk_advisor_recommend run.

Registering a new sk-code mode requires five JSON surfaces: mode-registry.json modes[] entry (with toolSurface, packetKind, backendKind, aliases, routingClass), extensions.surface-axis.surfaces, hub-router.json routerPolicy.tieBreak, a routerSignals entry with named classes, and vocabularyClasses keywords, plus leaf-manifest.json modes[] with a leaves array enumerating every packet file. Prose and fixtures follow: the SKILL.md sentence that declares itself the single source of truth for the surface count, two README passages repeating the count, a feature-catalog entry, a manual-testing-playbook scenario and row, a compiled-route-surface-hint test case, and the canary fixture plus its authored twin under specs/.

sk-code-ci is a surface packet, not a workflow mode: the hub defines surfaces as read-only domain-evidence packets (backendKind evidence-base, routingClass metadata, mutatesWorkspace false) bundled alongside a workflow mode and applied by the acting agent. Workflow YAML standards are consumed by authoring (sk-code-skilled) and review (sk-code-review), so they are evidence. Consequence that changes iteration 13's scaffold design: the packet's toolSurface forbids Write and Edit, so sk-code-ci cannot write a scaffolded workflow; its templates must be read-only assets that /doctor:ci scaffold fills.

Adding a fourth surface falsifies the SKILL.md sentence that states the hub has exactly three surfaces and two workflow modes and declares itself the single source of truth for every other sk-code doc that counts surfaces; two README passages repeat the count independently, so all three go stale in the same commit. Placement follows tieBreak with workflow modes first and surfaces after, SKILLED > OBSIDIAN > WEBFLOW, which puts sk-code-ci immediately after sk-code-skilled; whether /doctor:sk-code check 5l (documented as failing a surface placed after sk-code-skilled) applies to a built-in surface is inferred, not read.

The protected set can be defined by function instead of by remembered filenames: a workflow is protected when editing it can change whether another workflow may run or whether a credential is exposed, operationally (a) it is the sole enforcer of an invariant with no local gate (gate-inputs runs the checker tests, the real-tree check and every hook suite), (b) it holds a token-eligibility split (trigger-index-rebuild's rebuild/push separation keeps the write token in a job that runs no repository code), or (c) it is a guard whose failure invalidates other workflows' inputs (dispatch-enforcement-guard, naming-standard-guard). Protection means a second named confirmation, not immutability: protected workflows are reachable by customize, never by toggle.

Ownership splits because of mutatesWorkspace, not taste: sk-code-ci cannot write, while /doctor:ci toggle varies repository variables and customize edits workflow YAML, both of which the env router already does with a print-then-verify pattern. sk-git is not an alternative: its doctor surface is hooks/setup/standards scoped to .sk-git conventions with no CI route, so placing workflow standards there would make a git skill the GitHub Actions authority. Ruling: doctor owns list/check/toggle/customize, sk-code-ci owns standards, rule data, protected set and templates, and scaffold is the seam.

A first advisor-registry scan iterated entry dicts as if they were strings and reported zero doctor ids; re-running correctly returned 18 in each list. Recorded as an instance of the uniform-none failure mode.
